prompt:
Paint ONE finished frame of a film-like cutscene of our hand-painted point-and-click adventure game 'Posledny zvonec' (Slovakia; eras 1960, 1982, 1995, 2020, 2035). The reference images are numbered in the order they are given: Image 1: place reference: the real Rotunda interior (repaint it as the gallery) Image 2: reference for the subject of the mural: a Bratislava pedestrian underpass Image 3: character reference: Nina, 30, the curator Image 4: a finished interior painting from our game; use it only for the painting technique, brushwork, palette and line quality, not for its content

Shot: The 2035 Atlas exhibition gallery inside the real Rotunda building on the Chopok summit: a round room with big panoramic windows onto the mountains, temporary white gallery panels with framed works and soft spotlights. A large reproduction of a 1995 underpass mural hangs on a gallery panel: a painted night view of Petrzalka panel blocks, every lit window in a slightly different warm colour - amber, rose, pale green, gold - so that no two lights are the same. Nina stands beside it in her dark green coat, turned half to the viewer, one hand gesturing toward the windows of the mural as she explains it to a visitor.

Characters in this frame (briefs of the approved designs): Nina, a 30-year-old Slovak woman, curator of the Atlas memory exhibition in June 2035 and Ela's daughter: matter-of-fact, quick, clear about the limits of her authority. Straight dark brown hair, shoulder-length, worn loose with a side part and tucked behind one ear, a sharp intelligent face with a direct gaze. She wears a lightweight unlined dark bottle-green knee-length coat, open and unbuttoned, over a plain light grey crew-neck top, slim black trousers and simple white leather trainers. A service identification card hangs on a plain dark grey lanyard around her neck: a white card with a small photo square and a simple blue circle emblem, no readable text. Her arms hang relaxed at her sides. Ordinary clothes of the near future (alpine summer 2035), nothing futuristic, no logos, no face mask.

Light and time: Soft gallery spotlights, mountain daylight from the windows.

Character references show approved characters of the game on a plain grey card: copy each person's face, age, hair, body proportions, clothes and colours exactly, but pose and light them for this scene; never copy the grey card, the sheet layout or a duplicate of the same person. Place references show the real location and its painted version in our game: keep its architecture, materials and era. Photos are only references: repaint everything in our style, paint any real people in them out, and do not copy brand logos or shop names. Composition: a calm 16:9 picture like a still from the last minutes of a film, with a clear focal point and depth; it is shown whole with a caption below it, so keep the subject well inside the frame. One single image: no panels, no split screen, no border, no frame, no captions, no subtitles, no speech bubbles, no watermark, no UI, unless the shot asks for it. No text or lettering anywhere unless the shot quotes it exactly.

Style: classic 1990s hand-painted adventure game background. Rich painterly brushwork, slightly exaggerated cartoon proportions with gently curved lines, warm late-afternoon sunlight, saturated but harmonious colours, soft dappled shadows under the trees.
